# <!--name-->slack/notify-status<!--/name-->
<!--description-->
Post a color-coded Slack status notification for the current GitHub job or workflow.
Requires `permissions: id-token: write` in the calling workflow.
<!--/description-->

## Inputs
<!--inputs-->
| Name            | Description                                                                                                  | Required | Default |
|-----------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------|---------|
| `channel`       | Slack channel ID or name                                                                                     | `true`   | ` `     |
| `status`        | Status to report (success, failure, cancelled, or skipped). Defaults to the current job status when omitted. | `false`  | ` `     |
| `mention`       | Optional Slack user ID, subteam ID, or formatted mention token to include in the message                     | `false`  | ` `     |
| `description`   | Optional resolution notes, runbook links, or other supporting text                                           | `false`  | ` `     |
| `fail-on-error` | Fail the step when Slack delivery fails                                                                      | `false`  | `false` |
<!--/inputs-->

## Outputs
<!--outputs-->
| Name      | Description                                  |
|-----------|----------------------------------------------|
| `success` | Whether the message was posted successfully  |
| `channel` | Slack channel ID from the posted message     |
| `ts`      | Slack message timestamp for threaded replies |
<!--/outputs-->

## Usage
<!--usage action="your/action" version="v1"-->
```yaml
permissions:
  id-token: write

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: ./build.sh

      - if: always() && !cancelled()
        uses: elastic/docs-actions/slack/notify-status@v1
        with:
          channel: C0123456789
          status: ${{ job.status }}
          description: Nightly docs build
```
<!--/usage-->

## Conditional examples

Notify only on failure:

```yaml
- if: failure()
  uses: elastic/docs-actions/slack/notify-status@v1
  with:
    channel: C0123456789
    status: failure
    description: See https://example.com/runbook for recovery steps
    mention: S0123456789
```

Notify when the workflow is cancelled:

```yaml
- if: cancelled()
  uses: elastic/docs-actions/slack/notify-status@v1
  with:
    channel: C0123456789
    status: cancelled
```

Notify after every terminal outcome except cancellation:

```yaml
- if: always() && !cancelled()
  uses: elastic/docs-actions/slack/notify-status@v1
  with:
    channel: C0123456789
    status: ${{ job.status }}
```

## Multi-job workflow status

Use a dedicated notify job when the reported status should reflect multiple upstream jobs:

```yaml
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: ./build.sh

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: ./test.sh

  deploy:
    needs: [build, test]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: ./deploy.sh

  notify:
    needs: [build, test, deploy]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: elastic/docs-actions/slack/notify-status@v1
        with:
          channel: C0123456789
          status: >-
            ${{ contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') && 'failure'
                || contains(needs.*.result, 'cancelled') && 'cancelled'
                || 'success' }}
          description: Documentation deployment
          mention: S0123456789
```

## Notes

- Requires `elastic/docs-actions/slack/notify@v1` with attachment support (available from release 1.36.0 onward).
- When `status` is omitted, the action uses the current job status at invocation time.
- For soft failures created with `continue-on-error: true`, pass an explicit `status` derived from `steps.<id>.outcome` if you need the notification to reflect the failed step.
- Top-level text uses the repository and workflow name. The attachment shows status color, a normal status line, optional runbook text in smaller context styling, a workflow run button, optional cc mentions, and a GitHub repository footer. The elastic-docs-slack-notifier Lambda already adds Docs Bot attribution to posted messages.
- Messages use Block Kit metadata inside a colored Slack attachment. Slack still requires attachments for the status color bar.
- `mention` accepts Slack user IDs (`U…`), subteam IDs (`S…`), already-formatted tokens such as `<@U0123456789>`, or comma-separated combinations.

## Repository access

Workflows can only invoke the Slack notifier if their repository is on the OIDC allowlist in [docs-infra](https://github.com/elastic/docs-infra).

1. Add the repository to [`aws/elastic-web/eu-west-1/slack-notifier/repositories.yml`](https://github.com/elastic/docs-infra/blob/main/aws/elastic-web/eu-west-1/slack-notifier/repositories.yml):

   ```yaml
   repositories:
     - name: elastic/your-repo
   ```

2. Open a PR in `elastic/docs-infra`. Merging to `main` deploys the change through the terragrunt workflow.

3. In the calling workflow, set `permissions: id-token: write`.

Fork PRs do not receive OIDC tokens, so the action cannot authenticate from fork workflows.
